segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I'm Beth.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: One area of technology which has been in the news a lot recently is robotics the design and building of robots.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Humanoid robots, meaning robots which appear and behave like humans,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: are being built to help us do everything from washing the dishes to babysitting the kids.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: But not everyone feels comfortable with the idea of inviting a human-like robot into their home.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Neil, how would you feel about living with a robot?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I really don't want to live with a robot. I have enough people in my house.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: With advances in AI, robots are becoming smart enough to develop meaningful relationships with humans.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: There are reports of people telling their secrets to robot therapists and even falling in love with their robot friend.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: In this episode, we'll meet a home companion robot called Abby, who's making friends with the elderly residents of Melbourne in Australia.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And as usual, we'll learn some useful new vocabulary,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: all of which you'll find over on our website,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: First, I have a question for you, Beth.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Because it's important people feel safe around robots,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: engineers design them to look like the friendly characters seen in animated movies by studios like Pixar and Dreamworks So what is the name of Pixar friendly robot who picks up garbage on an

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: uninhabited planet Earth in the year 2805? Is it A, Ros, B, WALL-E or C, R2-D2?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I am pretty certain that the answer is B, WALL-E.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, we'll find out the answer later in the programme.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For five months during the Covid pandemic, Australian engineer Grace Brown had no human contact.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: She used this time to build a home companion robot, Abbey,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: with the idea it would provide companionship to other people suffering loneliness.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Now Grace runs her own company, Andromeda,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: building robots specially designed as company for elderly residents in care homes who don't get many visitors.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Here she explains more about Abby to BBC World Service programme The Conversation.

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: Abby, who's the humanoid robot that we build at Andromeda,

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: people don't expect humanoid robots to have like so much personality.

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: She's very, very sassy. She's very inquisitive and curious.

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: And I think when people meet her, they're always kind of taken back by,

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: oh, she's like got a mind of her own.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: When people meet Abby, they are surprised by her sassy personality.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: The adjective sassy means bold,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: confident and cheeky.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Some people are taken aback,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: meaning they are shocked or surprised

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: by the things Abi says She really seems to be interested and to take care of the people she meets Abby can also express opinions And Grace says she has a mind of her own a phrase used when

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: a non-living object, like a robot, seems to be behaving or acting independently of human control.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Unlike the unpredictable and violent robots which are sometimes portrayed in sci-fi movies,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Abby is much more approachable and friendly, even funny.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: She can blow bubbles from her hand.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Her softer design was a conscious decision by Grace,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: who wanted children and elderly people to interact with Abby naturally and without fear,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: as she explained to BBC World Service's The Conversation.

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: I originally modelled her off the size of a young child,

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: so a six, seven-year-old child, so she's about 110 centimetres tall.

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: She's got a whole splash of different colours.

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: She's got large, expressive eyes.

segments.speaker: Grace Brown
segments.text: I was very much trying to replicate the approachableness and the endearingness of these different Pixar characters that you'd watch in all of these films.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Abby looks like a friendly character from a Pixar film.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: She's the size of a six or seven-year-old child and decorated with a splash of colour,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: a phrase used when a bit of colour is added to brighten up something which is dull or unexciting.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Abby also has large, expressive eyes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: If you describe something as expressive,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: you mean it shows what someone thinks or feels.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Elderly residents who regularly chat with Abbey say the robot companion brings them joy and a sense of community

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well it is good to hear the positive side of technology

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: which can still seem a bit strange or frightening.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I would like to see Abby blowing bubbles from her hand.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Now, isn't it time you revealed the answer to your question, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I asked you for the name of Pixar's friendly robot

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: who picks up garbage on an uninhabited planet Earth in the year 2805.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I said it was Wally.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And you were correct.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That is the right answer.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned starting with humanoid,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: an adjective meaning to have the appearance and behaviour of a human.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Someone who is sassy, is bold, confident and cheeky.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If you are taken aback by something, you are shocked or surprised by it.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: If you say an object has a mind of its own,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: you mean that it seems to be acting independently, without human control.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: The phrase a splash of colour is used when a bit of colour

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: is added to brighten something which is dull or unexciting.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And finally, the adjective expressive means showing what someone thinks or feels.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Once again, our six minutes are up.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: If you've enjoyed this episode, then head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: where you'll find a quiz and worksheet to practice the vocabulary you've learnt.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: See you again soon, but for now, it's goodbye.

segments.speaker: Neil
